title: Coordinates from an admissible subalgebra
statement: Let k, Λ, p, q and n satisfy the hypotheses of lem-weil-pbc-popescu-flat-coordinates. Given a local subalgebra A₀ of B = Λ_q/(qΛ_q)^n that is Popescu-admissible for qB [def-weil-pbc-popescu-admissible-subalgebra], there is a local admissible subalgebra A of B with A₀ ≤ A, maximal ideal equal to the contraction of qB, and the polynomial coordinates, localized flat map, ideal equality and spanning residue differentials described in lem-weil-pbc-popescu-flat-coordinates. No finite set is an input or part of this conclusion.

proof.text: *The subring $A$ and the elements $\lambda$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo-choose] applied to $A_0$ there are an admissible $A\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ with $E\subseteq A_0\subseteq A$, residue field $F=A/\mathfrak m_A$ with $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$, elements $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_t\in\Lambda$ whose images in $\bar\Lambda$ lie in $A$ and whose residues $\bar\lambda_j\in F$ have differentials $\mathrm d\bar\lambda_1,\dots,\mathrm d\bar\lambda_t$ forming a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and elements $\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r\in\mathfrak q$ with images in $A$ which generate $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. Since $A$ is essentially of finite type over $k$, so is its quotient field $F$, which is therefore a finitely generated field extension of $k$ (generated by the images of finitely many algebra generators). (Stacks picks the $\lambda_j$ for the subring of step 3 directly; as recorded in [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo-choose], that is not possible for every such subring, which is why $A_0$ is enlarged.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Denote F = A/m_A the residue field so that k in F in K. Pick lambda_1,...,lambda_t in Lambda which map to elements of A in Lambda-bar such that moreover the images of d lambda_1,...,d lambda_t form a basis of Omega_{F/k}'

proof.text: *Flatness of the first part.* Let $\varphi':k[y_1,\dots,y_t]\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] send $y_j\mapsto\lambda_j$ and $\mathfrak p'=(\varphi')^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; since $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\cap\Lambda=\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak p'$ is also the inverse image of the maximal ideal under $k[y_1,\dots,y_t]\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-over-field-flat] (Stacks 07E6) to the Noetherian local $k$-algebra $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, geometrically regular over $k$ (step 1), the finitely generated subextension $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$ and this map (the image of $y_j$ in $K$ is $\bar\lambda_j\in F$, and the $\mathrm d\bar\lambda_j$ form a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$, step 4): $P'=k[y_1,\dots,y_t]_{\mathfrak p'}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $S:=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qS$ and residue field $K$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Consider the map phi': k[y_1..y_t] -> Lambda ... By More on Algebra, Lemma 07E6 the ring map k[y_1..y_t]_{p'} -> Lambda_q is flat and Lambda_q/p'Lambda_q is regular'

proof.text: *A regular system of parameters of $S$ from the $\lambda'_i$.* The images of $\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r$ generate $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 4), hence the maximal ideal $\mathfrak qS$ of $S$, hence span the $K$-vector space $\mathfrak qS/\mathfrak q^2S$. Choose among them $e$ elements whose images form a basis of $\mathfrak qS/\mathfrak q^2S$ and call them $\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m$ ($m=t+e$). By Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] their images generate $\mathfrak qS$, and no proper subset does, so they form a minimal set of generators of the maximal ideal of the regular local ring $S$, i.e. a regular system of parameters, and $e=\dim S$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] their images form a regular sequence in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and $S/(\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m)S=S/\mathfrak qS=K\ne0$. Each $\lambda_{t+i}$ lies in $\mathfrak q$ and its image in $\bar\Lambda$ lies in $A$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Thus we can choose further elements lambda_{t+1},...,lambda_m in Lambda which map into A in Lambda-bar and which map to a regular system of parameters of Lambda_q/p'Lambda_q'

proof.text: *The map $\varphi$ and $\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$.* Let $\varphi:k[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to\Lambda$, $y_j\mapsto\lambda_j$, extend $\varphi'$, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $P=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]_{\mathfrak p}$. Then $\mathfrak p\cap k[y_1,\dots,y_t]=\mathfrak p'$ and $y_{t+1},\dots,y_m\in\mathfrak p$ (as $\lambda_{t+i}\in\mathfrak q$). Since $\varphi(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; conversely $\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\supseteq\mathfrak p'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}+(\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, which is all of $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ because the images of $\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m$ generate $\mathfrak qS=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 6). So $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, the first half of (1).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'We obtain phi: k[y_1..y_m] -> Lambda having property (1)'

proof.text: *The closed fibre $P/\mathfrak p'P$.* Elements of $k[y_1,\dots,y_t]\setminus\mathfrak p'$ are not in $\mathfrak p$, so they are units of $P$; hence $P/\mathfrak p'P$ is the localization of $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[y_{t+1},\dots,y_m]$ ($\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ the fraction field of $k[y_1,\dots,y_t]/\mathfrak p'$) at the image $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ of $\mathfrak p$. As $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ contains the maximal ideal $(y_{t+1},\dots,y_m)$ (step 7) and is proper, it equals it. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-origin-regular-local] over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, $P/\mathfrak p'P$ is a regular local ring of dimension $e=m-t$ whose maximal ideal is generated by $y_{t+1},\dots,y_m$. $P'$, $P$ are Noetherian local rings (localizations [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] of polynomial rings over a field [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]), and $P'\to P$ (localization of the inclusion, $\mathfrak p\cap k[y_1,\dots,y_t]=\mathfrak p'$) and $P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ are local homomorphisms, with $\mathfrak m_{P'}P=\mathfrak p'P$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623) (the flatness in property (1), left implicit by Stacks; it repeats the end of the proof of More on Algebra, Lemma 07E6)

proof.text: *$P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat.* The induced local homomorphism $P/\mathfrak p'P\to S=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of Noetherian local rings sends the regular system of parameters $y_{t+1},\dots,y_m$ of the regular local ring $P/\mathfrak p'P$ (step 8) to $\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m$, a regular sequence in $S$ with nonzero quotient (step 6); so it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular] (Algebra 07DY). Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] (Algebra 00MP) to $P'\to P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and $M=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$: these are Noetherian local rings and local homomorphisms (steps 1, 8); $M$ is generated by $1$ and nonzero; $M/\mathfrak m_{P'}M=S$ is flat over $P/\mathfrak m_{P'}P=P/\mathfrak p'P$ (just shown); $M$ is flat over $P'$ (step 5). Hence $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $P$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. With step 7 this proves (1).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'We obtain phi having property (1)'; More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E6 (line 8885: 'We win by Algebra, Lemmas 00R4 and 00NQ')

proof.text: The first $t$ coordinate residues have differentials forming a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo-choose]. Appending the parameter coordinates leaves their span equal to the whole differential module [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The enlarged admissible subalgebra still contains $E$. Its maximal ideal is the contraction of $JB$, because admissibility puts its maximal ideal inside that proper contraction, and maximality gives equality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_popescu_flat_coordinates_given_admissible
    (k : Type u) (Λ : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (hreg : IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ) (q : Ideal Λ) [q.IsPrime]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (A₀ : Subalgebra k (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
      (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)) (_ : IsLocalRing A₀)
    (hA₀ : A₀.IsPopescuAdmissible ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))).map
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)))) :
    ∃ (A : Subalgebra k (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
        (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)) (_ : IsLocalRing A),
      A.IsPopescuAdmissible ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))).map
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n))) ∧
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A = Ideal.comap A.val.toRingHom
        ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))).map
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n))) ∧
      A₀ ≤ A ∧
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
        (ψ : Localization.AtPrime (q.comap φ.toRingHom) →+* Localization.AtPrime q),
        ψ.comp (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
            (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap φ.toRingHom))) =
          (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp φ.toRingHom ∧
        q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) =
          (q.comap φ.toRingHom).map
            ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp φ.toRingHom) ∧
        ψ.Flat ∧
        ∃ a : Fin m → A,
          (∀ j, (a j : Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
            (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n) =
            Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)
              (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (φ (MvPolynomial.X j)))) ∧
          Submodule.span (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
            (Set.range (fun j ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
              (IsLocalRing.residue A (a j)))) = ⊤
